schemaVersion: 1

name: retries-and-backoff
version: 1.1.4
description: >-
  Retry as a policy with a cost: classifying a failure as transient, permanent or ambiguous
  before retrying anything; why a timeout is ambiguous and safe to retry only under
  idempotency or reconciliation; capped jittered backoff; aggregate retry budgets plus
  per-call limits; one layer owning the end-to-end policy; and
  honouring 429, Retry-After and the remaining deadline. Use when a catch block retries on
  Exception or on a message substring, when backoff has no jitter, when several layers each
  retry the same call, when a POST is retried after a timeout, when a dependency's inbound
  rate rises as its success rate falls, when a retry sleeps inside a transaction, or when
  duplicates appear after an outage. Does not cover making the operation safe to repeat
  (idempotency), the bound itself (timeouts-and-deadlines), tripping
  (circuit-breakers), retry storms (cascading-failures), load shedding
  (rate-limiting-and-load-shedding), or the exception type (java-exception-design).

  codex:
    interface:
      display_name: Retries And Backoff
      short_description: Classifying failures, jitter and retry budgets
      default_prompt: Use Retries And Backoff to decide whether this failure should be retried and at what cost.

scopeAndCriteria.promise: Classify whether another attempt is useful and safe, then bound attempts, timing and aggregate load for the same intent.
scopeAndCriteria.activation: Untyped/unconditional retries, absent jitter, nested amplification, ambiguous writes, held resources, overload and retry policy review.
scopeAndCriteria.role: Explanation, review and bounded policy implementation; a narrow answer need not create new retry infrastructure.
scopeAndCriteria.exclusions: Creating idempotency guarantees, defining the outer timeout itself, circuit-tripping implementation, system-wide storm control, exception-type design.
scopeAndCriteria.decisiveEvidence: Transport/application outcome contract, stable intent and payload, caller deadline, actual nested policy, response/resource lifecycle, scoped counters, deployed versions.
scopeAndCriteria.authoringBaseline: Standalone helper Java 17; pattern-switch loop Java 21, explicitly conceptual; Spring Retry 2.0.12 and Resilience4j 2.3.0 version-specific discussion.
scopeAndCriteria.targetBaseline: The applying project must inspect actual toolchains/dependencies and configuration; this review authorizes no upgrades.

findingsPreserved.assessment: Outcome evidence and operation semantics control retryability. Transient certifies safe replay; unknown writes remain durable unknown until an authoritative same-intent result.
findingsPreserved.consequencePrevented: Neither a timeout, a retryable-looking status nor a key alone establishes a failed operation or safe new effect.
findingsPreserved.support: RFC 9110 semantics, source review and local unknown-state/terminal/budget controls.

findingsPreserved.assessment: Helper saturates arithmetic and validates durations; loop gates entry, recomputes remaining time after delay, respects advised delay and propagates interruption.
findingsPreserved.consequencePrevented: Overflow, early retry against server guidance, attempts after known deadline/interrupt and loss of unresolved status.
findingsPreserved.support: Exact extracted snippets compiled at declared language releases; 12 jitter cases and 13 loop scenarios pass.

findingsPreserved.assessment: Per-call limits, aggregate scope, burst/refill and matching measurement windows are distinct; illustrative multiplication is conditional.
findingsPreserved.consequencePrevented: Calling a process bucket fleet-wide or inferring actual amplification from configuration alone.
findingsPreserved.support: Static review of formulas, scopes, caveats and proportional validation instructions; no fleet measurement claimed.

findingsPreserved.assessment: Versioned library predicates, recovery, randomization, proxy invocation and ambient REQUIRED transaction are qualified instead of inferred from annotations.
findingsPreserved.consequencePrevented: Broad exception retry despite narrow predicate, wrong caller-visible recovery exception, mistaken full jitter, or retained transaction during backoff.
findingsPreserved.support: Pinned Spring Retry 2.0.12 and Resilience4j 2.3.0 sources inspected; no framework runtime test.

findingsPreserved.assessment: Request reproducibility is separate from business replay safety; failed response bodies have bounded cleanup before another attempt.
findingsPreserved.consequencePrevented: Reusing exhausted or changed payload sources and indefinitely draining error bodies.
findingsPreserved.support: Java 17 BodyPublisher and BodySubscribers contracts inspected.

noChangeRationale: The complete package already contains the decision conditions, alternatives and failure-path guards material to this review. Primary sources and targeted examples did not reveal an in-scope defect; extra instructions would duplicate existing guidance. This is bounded preservation, not certification that no defect exists.
capabilitiesPreserved: Transient/permanent/ambiguous classification and authoritative reconciliation for unknown writes.
Stable intent plus repeatable payload; no retry after response delivery without an explicit resumable contract.
Full-jitter arithmetic, server minimum, deadline recheck and cancellation/actual-completion distinction.
Single end-to-end owner, nested attempt accounting and scoped retry budgets with explicit initial/refill behavior.
Fresh transactional state and ambient transaction/proxy caveats.
Deliberate retry/breaker composition and versioned framework recovery/predicate behavior.
Evidence-limited incident interpretation, bounded metric labels and proportional validation/no-change outcomes.
All four files, examples, sources, metadata and routing unchanged byte-for-byte.
